newsitem.title: USA: U.S. five-year TIPS receive less-than-warm welcome.
newsitem.headline: U.S. five-year TIPS receive less-than-warm welcome.

text.p: The first-ever five-year U.S. Treasury inflation-protected note received a less-than-warm welcome in the government securities market Wednesday, as most players showed little interest in the new issue.
But the weak results offered no big suprises.

"They came and went. Now it is time to move on to bigger and better things," said Neil DeSarno, head government bond trader at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp. "I have not heard anyone saying, 'I have got to have these.'"

The issue fetched a yield of 3.744 percent, well above the 3.54 percent the when-issued five-year note closed at on Monday. By late Wednesday, the issue had improved somewhat to 3.67 percent, indicating solid distribution, traders said.
Over the past two sessions, market participants said the TIPS were too expensive given low inflation levels and inflationary expectations.
Still, some were more optimistic about the results.
"The issue performed fairly well considering the negative feelings of the past couple of days," said William Lloyd, head of bond market research at BZW Securities Inc.
Some market participants pointed to the 3.31 bid-to-cover ratio as a positive.
Wednesday's auction marked the third set of TIPS auctioned by the Treasury. The issue was awarded at the highest yield ever seen for a TIPS issue.
Traders said higher yields appeared to be the trend for new TIPS issues until renewed fears of rising inflation emerge.

The new five-year issue will mature in 2002 and carries a coupon of 3.625 percent. The base Consumer Price Index for the issue was 160.154. The issue will pay coupons in January and July, starting on January 15, 1998.
